clue.text: Cast in the short series

indicators.note: short means the word the is cut off before its final letter

parts.note: the word the, written out
a row is a series of things in a line

explanation.surface: A remark about the cast of a short-running series.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast a ball or a net is to fling it, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Wheel in best English novelist

indicators.note: in means the wheel sits inside the word for best

parts.note: top means best, as in top quality
to wheel something can mean to roll it

explanation.surface: Praise for the finest English novelist, wheeled out once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Trollope was a Victorian English novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope wrote the Barsetshire novels, so he is an example of a novelist.

clue.text: Reasonable grounds, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for grounds goes

parts.note: a rationale is the grounds or reasoning for a course of action

explanation.surface: Grounds that are, for the most part, sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational and reasonable both mean based on sound logic, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Squeaky-clean Heather, with twin otherwise

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so these three words are rearranged together

explanation.surface: A girl called Heather is spotless, unlike her twin sister.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from washing-powder adverts and means morally spotless, entirely beyond reproach.

clue.text: Huge mobile amplifier

parts.note: mega is slang for huge or enormous
a mobile is a mobile phone

explanation.surface: An enormous portable loudspeaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud-hailer is a hand-held device that amplifies the voice, so it is a kind of amplifier.

clue.text: Help to support married servant

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece stands below, so the help goes under the married

parts.note: aid means help

explanation.surface: Assistance given to keep a married domestic in work.
explanation.definitionFit: A maid is a female domestic servant.

clue.text: See actress in great cocktail dress before start of Oscars

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of great are mixed up

parts.note: garb means dress or clothing

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, taken here from Oscars

explanation.surface: Look at a film star in a smart cocktail dress before the Academy Awards begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link inviting the solver to look; GREAT rearranges to GRETA.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood film star, an example of an actress.

clue.text: I can stop the traffic in bird interbreeding

parts.note: a pelican is a large water bird
crossing is breeding two different varieties together

explanation.surface: A cross-bred bird claims it can bring traffic to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: A pelican crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with lights the walker controls; the definition speaks as the crossing itself.
explanation.definitionFit: This light-controlled road crossing lets pedestrians press a button that halts the traffic, so it can stop vehicles.

clue.text: Business suit

definitions.meaning: a firm or organisation, as in a small engineering concern
a set of clothes worn together

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a company or team and a set of clothes worn together.

clue.text: Sinful, eastern bishop and social worker

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
the ant is a social insect and a proverbial worker

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing pinned on an Eastern bishop and a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a welfare officer but an ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means straying from proper conduct, hence erring or sinful.

clue.text: Unsafe in hot volatile French city

indicators.note: volatile means unstable and changeable, so the letters of in and hot are thrown into a new order

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Hot weather making a French city dangerous and unstable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volatile' rearranges IN HOT into ONTHI, which runs straight into NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Skating where the ice is thin is risky, so the idiom means in a precarious, unsafe position.

clue.text: Following behind, close to mother

parts.note: running behind means running late

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, here taken from mother

explanation.surface: Someone trailing just behind, staying near their mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Following and subsequent are both senses of coming afterwards in time, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Boy in deli one liked

indicators.note: in signals that the name sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A lad in a delicatessen took a fancy to someone there.
explanation.definitionFit: A common male first name, so a crossword-style example of a boy.

clue.text: Support coercive measure

definitions.meaning: to approve or authorise something officially
a penalty imposed to force compliance, such as trade restrictions on a state

explanation.definitionFit: The word famously carries two opposite senses: official approval and a punitive measure.

clue.text: Shakes with muesli and the like?

definitions.meaning: waves something about menacingly, as a weapon
..., read as two words, are breakfast foods such as muesli

explanation.surface: Someone trembles over breakfast cereals.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish is to wave or shake something, such as a sword, in a threatening way.

clue.text: Hypocrite may make accusation about plants

indicators.note: about means going round, so the accusation is wrapped around the plants

parts.note: a plaint is a formal complaint or charge in law
asters are daisy-like garden flowers

explanation.surface: A fake might make a charge concerning the plants in a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the accusation round the plants; 'may make' is only a link. A plaster saint is a statue of a saint, hence someone who looks virtuous.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone posing as morally spotless, like a pious plaster statue, is a self-righteous pretender, a hypocrite.

clue.text: Hector having left the stage, start play again

parts.note: to hector is to bully
an actor who has left the stage is off

explanation.surface: Once the bully has gone from the stage, the game can restart.
explanation.walkthrough: A bully-off is how a hockey game is started or restarted, two players clashing sticks over the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In field hockey this procedure starts or resumes play, so it means restarting the game.

clue.text: Quiet and revolutionary, the German piece of office equipment

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
red is a common word for a revolutionary or communist
der is the German masculine form of the

explanation.surface: A silent German revolutionary working in an office.
explanation.definitionFit: A shredder cuts documents into strips, an example of office machinery.

clue.text: Painter defeats sitting member in town?

parts.note: in a British election, a party that ousts the sitting MP is said to gain the seat, so it gains
a borough is a town with its own corporation

explanation.surface: An election result: a candidate unseats the incumbent in some town.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gainsborough was an 18th-century English portrait and landscape painter; the question mark admits that Gainsborough is also a real Lincolnshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Gainsborough is a famous English painter, so the name is an example of one.

clue.text: Garment of hide

definitions.meaning: a cloth wrapped round a corpse for burial
to cover or conceal, as in mist veiling a hill

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a burial sheet and to veil or conceal something.

clue.text: School founder shown in marble, with name underneath

indicators.note: in a down clue the name sits under the marble

parts.note: an alley is a large playing marble

explanation.surface: A school founder's name carved beneath a marble memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Alleyn, the Elizabethan actor, founded Dulwich College in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Alleyn founded Dulwich College in 1619, so he is a school founder.

clue.text: Worthily translated the Scriptures

indicators.note: translated means changed into another form, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has done a worthy job of rendering the Bible into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy writ is an old name for sacred writings, chiefly the Bible.

clue.text: I succeeded elderly European queen

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded
elderly means old

explanation.surface: A ruler announcing that she followed an aged European queen to the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: Isolde is the Irish queen of the Tristan legend and Wagner's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the Irish princess and queen of Arthurian romance, an example of a queen.

clue.text: Youngster in heart of Arabian Desert?

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, taken from Arabian

parts.note: to rat is to desert, as a rat leaves a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A child lost in the middle of the Arabian desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' is not the sandy noun but the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Brat is an informal, usually disparaging word for a child.

clue.text: Signs in old bishop, then priest

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: Omens seen in an old bishop and then a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeli are the dagger-shaped marks used in printing as reference signs.

clue.text: Daring shown by real outlaw crossing one

indicators.note: crossing means lying across, so the one goes between the other pieces

parts.note: hard, as in hard facts or hard cash, means real and tangible
Robin Hood is the archetypal outlaw, so hood stands for one
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Bravery displayed by a genuine outlaw going across alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' places the one between the other two pieces rather than inside either; 'real' is hard in the sense of hard facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardihood is boldness or audacity, a noun synonym for daring.

clue.text: Secret society formed after reverend's last service

indicators.note: after means the society comes after the reverend's final letter
the last of a word is its final letter, here from reverend's

parts.note: inner, as in an inner circle, means private and hidden
a set is a social group or circle

explanation.surface: A clandestine group is founded after a clergyman's final church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' is not a church service but a set of matching crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner service is a matched collection of plates and dishes for the table.

clue.text: Errand boy in forge, working

indicators.note: working means being worked or processed, so the letters of forge are reshaped

explanation.surface: A boy employed to run errands at a blacksmith's forge.
explanation.definitionFit: A gofer is someone sent to go for things, a junior who runs errands.
